topic:
The nor'easter hitting the US East Coast this weekend (Sept 26-27, 2026). It is a RAIN, WIND and COASTAL FLOODING storm (NO snow, NO blizzard). VERIFIED FACTS ONLY (AP via Spokesman-Review, CNN, NBC News, PhillyVoice, all Sept 26, 2026):
- New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency and told people to avoid travel through the weekend.
- Flooding in Atlantic City, New Jersey, reached its highest point since Superstorm Sandy; neighborhoods along the Jersey Shore were flooded.
- Waves crashed over seawalls; wind gusts forecast up to 60 mph and breaking waves up to 9 feet.
- First responders rescued 9 adults and 1 dog from flooded motels in New Jersey on Saturday morning.
- Tens of thousands of people in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic lost power; trees came down in New York City.
- As of Saturday afternoon, no deaths had been reported.
- The National Weather Service said the storm would intensify again Saturday night into Sunday, with more flooding likely.
Story order: what's happening → the emergencies → Atlantic City flooding (highest since Sandy) → the rescues → outages and trees → what comes Sunday. Do NOT mention snow, blizzards, bombogenesis, deaths or flight numbers. Photos: coastal flooding, waves over a seawall, flooded shore streets, downed trees in New York City, storm clouds over the Atlantic.
